notes: Sample edition with illustrative stories. Real news arrives after the first scheduled run.

brief.headline: RBI holds the repo rate and signals room to cut if inflation stays low
brief.sowhat: Loan rates may ease later this year; rate-sensitive sectors like NBFCs and real estate react first.

brief.headline: Sample: Kirana-tech startup raises $40M Series C to expand to 30 cities
brief.sowhat: Large B2B commerce rounds are back, a sign growth investors are returning to Indian retail tech.

brief.headline: Sample: Steelmakers raise prices for a third month as import curbs bite
brief.sowhat: Better margins for steel companies, higher costs for carmakers and builders.

jargon.meaning: A temporary extra tax on imports to protect domestic industry from a sudden surge.

business.headline: Sample: Steelmakers raise prices for a third month as import curbs bite
business.summary: Major steel producers increased prices again this month. A safeguard duty on cheap imports has reduced competition from overseas suppliers.
business.why: Margins improve for steel firms, while auto, appliance and construction companies face higher input costs.

jargon.meaning: Capital expenditure: money spent on long-term assets like plants.

business.headline: Sample: Conglomerate plans ₹30,000 crore green hydrogen investment over five years
business.summary: The group said it will build electrolyser capacity and a hydrogen hub in phases. The first phase is due in two years.
business.why: Shows how large groups are steering capex into energy transition; watch for supplier and PLI tie-ups.

jargon.meaning: Foreign portfolio investors: overseas funds buying Indian stocks and bonds.

business.headline: Sample: Foreign investors turn net buyers of Indian shares this month
business.summary: Overseas portfolio investors bought more Indian stocks than they sold, after several months of selling.
business.why: Steady FPI inflows usually support large banks and IT stocks and the rupee.

business.headline: Sample: Private bank's loan growth slows as it tightens unsecured lending
business.summary: The lender reported slower growth in personal loans and credit cards after raising its approval standards.
business.why: Signals banks are still cautious on unsecured credit after regulatory warnings.

jargon.meaning: The rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to banks.
The RBI panel that votes on interest rates.

policy.headline: RBI holds the repo rate and signals room to cut if inflation stays low
policy.summary: The Monetary Policy Committee kept the key lending rate unchanged. It said a cut is possible if inflation stays comfortably within its target.
policy.why: Borrowing costs could fall later; banks may reprice home and business loans.

policy.headline: Sample: Cabinet clears rules for new labour codes; states to notify next
policy.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the rules needed to put the labour codes into effect. States must issue their own notifications.
policy.why: Hiring costs, gig-worker benefits and compliance change for most employers.

jargon.meaning: The body of central and state finance ministers that sets GST rates.

policy.headline: Sample: GST Council to review rates on insurance and EV parts
policy.summary: The Council's next meeting will discuss lowering GST on some insurance products and electric-vehicle components.
policy.why: Could cut prices for buyers and change demand for insurers and EV makers.

global.headline: Sample: US Federal Reserve keeps rates steady, hints at one more cut
global.summary: The Fed left its policy rate unchanged and said it expects one further cut if inflation keeps easing.
global.why: Lower US rates tend to draw foreign money into emerging markets like India.

global.headline: Sample: Oil slips as major producers signal higher output
global.summary: Crude prices fell after producer nations indicated they may raise supply next quarter.
global.why: Cheaper oil lowers India's import bill and helps keep inflation in check.

vc.pulse: Sample: capital is concentrating in B2B commerce, fintech infrastructure and climate tech, while consumer apps see smaller rounds. Expect more down-round and secondary activity in late-stage consumer names.

deals.oneLiner: Supplies inventory and credit to neighbourhood stores

jargon.meaning: A later-stage round to scale a proven business.
Short-term money a business needs to buy stock and run day to day.

stories.headline: Sample: Kirana-tech startup raises $40M Series C to expand to 30 cities
stories.summary: The company, which supplies inventory and working-capital credit to small stores, raised a Series C led by a US growth investor. It plans to enter 30 more cities.
stories.why: A sizeable growth round in B2B commerce suggests investors see a path to profitability in serving India's small retailers.

jargon.meaning: Draft Red Herring Prospectus: the first IPO filing with SEBI.
Existing shareholders sell shares; money goes to them.

stories.headline: Sample: Quick-commerce firm files DRHP for a ₹4,000 crore IPO
stories.summary: The company filed its draft IPO papers with SEBI. The issue includes new shares and an offer for sale by early investors.
stories.why: A public-market test of loss-making consumer tech, and a chance for early VCs to return cash (DPI).

jargon.meaning: The first point at which a fund accepts commitments and can start investing.

stories.headline: Sample: Seed fund announces ₹400 crore first close of its second fund
stories.summary: The firm raised commitments mainly from domestic family offices and institutions. It will back about 30 seed-stage startups.
stories.why: More domestic LP money means Indian seed funds rely less on global cycles.

jargon.meaning: Months a company can operate before its cash runs out.

stories.headline: Sample: Edtech unicorn lays off 300 staff to extend its runway
stories.summary: The company cut jobs across sales and content teams. It said the move would make it profitable within 18 months.
stories.why: A classic runway story: cost cuts ahead of a possible next round or IPO.

dealOfDay.title: Sample: KiranaTech's $40M Series C
dealOfDay.whatHappened: A B2B platform serving neighbourhood stores raised $40M led by a US growth fund. It plans to expand to 30 cities and grow its credit book.
thesis: Investors are likely betting that bundling credit with inventory locks in stores and lifts margins.
They may see a large, under-digitised market of millions of small retailers.
Data from orders could make lending safer and cheaper over time.
risks: Credit losses if small stores struggle to repay.
Competition from large e-commerce and FMCG companies' own distribution.
Thin margins in distribution if lending doesn't scale.
askFounder: What is your contribution margin per store after credit losses?
How do retention and order frequency differ for stores that use credit?
What share of revenue comes from your top 3 cities?
dealOfDay.concept: Contribution margin after credit losses: in lending-led commerce, unit economics must include defaults, not just delivery and product costs.

ai.headline: Sample: A step-by-step guide to packaging a workflow as a Claude Skill
ai.summary: A developer walks through writing a SKILL.md file, adding an example and uploading the zip.
ai.why: Exactly the next step on the Skill Lab ladder.
ai.tryThis: Turn your case-interview note format into a skill this week.

ai.headline: Sample: Browser agents can now work across several tabs at once
ai.summary: A new update lets the assistant read and act across multiple open tabs for research tasks.
ai.why: Makes comparison research (funds, competitors) much faster.
ai.tryThis: Compare five seed funds' websites in one prompt and build a table.

jargon.meaning: Model Context Protocol: an open standard for connecting AI apps to tools and data.

ai.headline: Sample: How remote MCP servers connect AI assistants to business apps
ai.summary: An explainer on how connectors use the Model Context Protocol to reach tools like Drive and Notion.
ai.why: Foundation for Level 3: connecting Claude to your own data.
ai.tryThis: Connect Google Drive in Claude and ask it to summarise your PE notes.

insider.headline: Sample: Why seed funds need more shots on goal than they think
insider.summary: An investor uses simple maths to show how the power law shapes portfolio size and reserves.
insider.why: Explains the logic behind fund sizes you see in the news.
insider.takeaway: Ownership in the one outlier matters more than avoiding losers.

insider.headline: Sample: What makes a great board member at Series A
insider.summary: A founder-turned-VC describes how the best investors help without micromanaging.
insider.why: Useful context for how VCs add value after the cheque.
insider.takeaway: Help on hiring and the next round matters more than weekly advice.

xPost: Third new-age IPO filing this quarter. The real question isn't the valuation, it's whether quick-commerce unit economics hold once the discount war cools. (sample)
